quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This takes just a few minutes and helps you find problems before you ride.

questions.question: Where should your feet be when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: It is a good idea to drag your feet.
Your toes should be pointed downward.
You should keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
You should try to keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests for balance. Do not drag your feet or point your toes down, as this can catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: Which item is NOT a good choice for riding clothes?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles
A baseball cap to cover your hair

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a jacket and long pants made of sturdy material, boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and leather gloves. A baseball cap does not protect you and is not an acceptable substitute for a helmet.

questions.question: What should you check during a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: The general wear and tread of your tires
The amount of cushion your seat has

questions.correctAnswerText: The general wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, lights, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Not allowing a passenger on the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most effective way to reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wet pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are slippery surfaces. Ride with extra caution on these surfaces.

questions.question: What do goggles protect when riding?

options.text: Protect your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
Protect your face, but not your eyes.
Are not as effective at protecting your eyes as eyeglasses.
Are not effective in providing any protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. Only a face shield protects your entire face. Eyeglasses do not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you're planning to increase your speed.
Only when there is a lot of traffic.
Any time you plan on changing lanes.
Only if it is dark outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you plan on changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: On which surface does a motorcycle have the best traction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Dry pavement provides the best traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, and metal covers are more hazardous.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: Allows the wearer to see as far to the sides as is necessary for safe riding.
Does not have a chin strap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows the wearer to see as far to the sides as is necessary for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. It allows you to see everything you need for safe riding.

questions.question: During a pre-ride check, make sure:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes rub slightly when you steer.
Each brake can stop the motorcycle by itself.
Only the rear brake can stop the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can stop the motorcycle by itself.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before every ride. Each one should feel firm and stop the motorcycle when you squeeze it fully.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear is also called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Engine braking.
questions.explanation: When you shift to a lower gear, it slows down your motorcycle like using the brakes. That is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: If a friend has drunk too much and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take their keys.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has drunk too much to ride. Stop them any way you can, including taking their keys. Help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car:

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You discourage other drivers from passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car so the driver sees you in their rearview mirror. Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirror.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces are slippery for motorcycle tires. These include wet roads, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates. Dry pavement is the safest.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle straight up and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: Riding next to a car:

options.text: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
Is only dangerous when the road is wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride directly next to another vehicle. You may be in the driver's blind spot, and the vehicle blocks your way to escape.

questions.question: The only way your body removes alcohol is through:
questions.correctAnswerText: Time.
questions.explanation: Your body can only remove alcohol by passing time. Nothing else speeds up this process. There is no quick way to sober up.

questions.question: Keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead:

options.text: When stopping will be harder than normal.
When you want to see the scenery.
To invite other drivers to cut in front of you.
So the driver ahead does not know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When stopping will be harder than normal.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if your motorcycle needs more time to stop. This includes slippery pavement, poor visibility, or heavy traffic where another driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: If you think your motorcycle will take longer than usual to stop, what should you do?

options.text: Stay farther away from the vehicle in front of you.
Stay closer to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the vehicle in front of you.
questions.explanation: Stay farther away from other vehicles when your motorcycle takes longer to stop. This extra distance gives you more time to react and stop safely.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Slow down so other vehicles can pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: You cannot see blind spots using only your mirrors. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles before you change lanes.

questions.question: What material should you look for in a protective jacket or pants?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs while riding. Leather provides the best protection in a crash.

questions.question: If your shoes have laces, what should you do with them while riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Tuck them in.
questions.explanation: Tuck your shoelaces in securely while riding. Loose laces can catch on your motorcycle and cause an accident.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, why should you ride in the left portion of your lane?

options.text: It helps you see farther ahead.
It makes it hard to see the vehicle you are passing.
It allows the other driver to speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you see farther ahead.
questions.explanation: Riding in the left portion of your lane helps you see farther ahead and makes you more visible to drivers in the passing lane.
